newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FOCUS-Challenges seen ahead for Air NZ.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Challenges seen ahead for Air NZ.

text.p: Air New Zealand faces challenges ahead after announcing a 13.4 percent decline in earnings to NZ$225.2 million for the June 1996 year, analysts and brokers said on Monday.
Air NZ said it would be difficult to maintain earnings at or above the 1996 outcome, thanks to intense competition in both the domestic and international markets.
The somewhat uncertain outlook may help to support the logic behind the company's plan to buy TNT Ltd's 50 percent stake in Ansett Airlines Ltd, some brokers said.
Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board is expected to make its decision on the Ansett-Air NZ deal soon.

"You've got to grow your own market somewhere," BZW's Nigel Scott said. "They are not going to grow it domestically from New Zealand and they are not going to grow it internationally either, at the end of the day. So yes, it is justification (for the Ansett purchase)."

The next six months were going to be tough for Air NZ as it embarked on an ambitious NZ$100 million cost-cutting drive. Air NZ was no different to other airlines such as Qantas which were also seeking cost savings to boost earnings.
"People are looking for cost reductions to boost the bottom line from here on in, so it's really showing that it's a tough period they are going through," Scott said.
The Ansett deal would bring the combined benefits of cost savings on both sides of the Tasman through sharing of maintenance and terminal facilities, Scott said.
Patrick Russel at Hendry Hay McIntosh said the result was marginally below expectations in terms of operating earnings, although the bottom line profit was in synch with forecasts.
He said it was possible the national flag carrier had formed its bearish outlook before cut-price competitor Kiwi International struck difficulties.
"In light of what has happened with Kiwi, it may prove to be an overly conservative assumption," Russel said.
Kiwi last week made 90 of its 250 staff redundant in a major restructuring, and is involved in a legal dispute with Singapore's Region Air from which it leases an Airbus.
Russel said Kiwi's problems highlighted the need for the Ansett deal. "It calls for some sort of rationalisatiion in the industry and we are seeing part of that occur with what is happening to Kiwi."
But David Copley, Air NZ analyst at Cavill White Securities, said there were two schools of thought on Ansett.

"Ansett may provide the extra capacity and growth to help sustain Air NZ as an international airline," he said. "But then you could say, why add more airline assets at a time when airlines are coming under pressure?"
While the result was satisfactory, the outlook was "wobbly".
"Across the board, I don't think it looks that positive, especially given they're wanting to get into Ansett, which is a bit of an uncertainty in itself," Copley said.
Long-term, however, the Ansett purchase should be a positive. "It needs some sort of size in there and that's obviously the way the international airline market is going."
By 1.30 p.m. (0130 GMT), Air NZ "A" shares were down two cents at NZ$3.16. Air NZ "B" shares were untraded.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
